Empirical Research Plan: Threshold–Based Treatment Assignment

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Method: Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Rationale  
• The research question explicitly concerns treatment assignment determined by a cutoff.  
• RDD exploits the discontinuity in the probability of treatment at the threshold to recover the local average treatment effect (LATE) for units “just” on either side of the cutoff.  
• If the rule is strictly enforced (everyone on one side is treated), we implement a sharp RDD; if compliance is imperfect, we implement a fuzzy RDD using the cutoff as an instrument for actual treatment.  

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control Definition
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Running variable (X): continuously-measured assignment variable (e.g., household income, test score).  
• Cutoff (c): predetermined threshold that governs eligibility.  

Sharp RDD  
 Treatment indicator (T) = 1{X ≥ c}.  
 Control group = observations with X < c (within a chosen bandwidth).  

Fuzzy RDD  
 First stage: Zi = 1{X ≥ c} (eligibility).  
 Actual treatment Ti may differ from Zi; use Zi as an instrument.

Timing  
For cross-sectional data the “event date” is implicit; for panels we use the first period in which the threshold rule is active and restrict the window to observations near c.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes: In the absence of treatment, E[Y0|X] is continuous at X = c.  
 Plausibility: Institutional rules typically create an arbitrary cut; nothing else should change discontinuously there.

A2. No precise manipulation of X: Agents cannot sort with fine precision around the cutoff.  
 Plausibility: Hard for individuals to manipulate pre-treatment income or test scores at the exact threshold, but must be tested.

A3. Local independence: Covariates and unobservables evolve smoothly through c.  
 Plausibility: Reasonable if rule is exogenous.

A4. (If fuzzy) Exclusion & monotonicity: The cutoff affects outcomes only through treatment and no “defiers.”  
 Plausibility: Standard in RD; check by institutional knowledge.

A5. Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption (SUTVA).  
 Plausibility: Usually satisfied; must argue no spillovers exactly at c.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats & Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Threat 1. Sorting/manipulation of X  
 Test: McCrary density test; visual histogram.  
 Fix: Donut RD (drop data very close to c), tighter bandwidths.

Threat 2. Other policies or variables discontinuous at c  
 Test: Covariate balance checks and placebo outcomes.  
 Fix: Control for discontinuous covariates or redefine window.

Threat 3. Functional form & bandwidth sensitivity  
 Test: Estimate with multiple bandwidth selectors (Imbens–Kalyanaraman, CCT) and polynomial orders ≤2.  
 Fix: Report robust local linear estimates + bias-correction (Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(rdrobust)     # Main RD estimation
library(rddensity)    # McCrary test
library(fixest)       # For IV if fuzzy
set.seed(123)

# 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("threshold_data.csv")    # assume columns: id, X, T, Y, cov1, cov2

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------------
cutoff <- 0          # change if necessary
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Z = if_else(X >= cutoff, 1, 0),  # eligibility (instrument, sharp indicator)
    running = X - cutoff             # center on cutoff for convenience
  )

# 3a. Sharp RD -------------------------------------------------------------
sharp <- rdrobust(y = df$Y, x = df$running,
                  c = 0, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
summary(sharp)

# 3b. Fuzzy RD (if imperfect compliance) -----------------------------------
fuzzy <- rdrobust(y = df$Y, x = df$running, fuzzy = df$T,
                  c = 0, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
summary(fuzzy)

# 4. Density test ----------------------------------------------------------
rdensity <- rddensity(df$running, c = 0)
summary(rdensity)
plot(rdensity)

# 5. Covariate balance (placebo) ------------------------------------------
rdrobust(y = df$cov1, x = df$running, c = 0)

# 6. Robustness: alternative bandwidth (CCT) ------------------------------
bw_cct <- rdbwselect(y = df$Y, x = df$running, c = 0)$bws[1]   # CCT bw
robust_alt <- rdrobust(y = df$Y, x = df$running, c = 0, h = bw_cct)
summary(robust_alt)

# 7. Donut RD (drop |running| < 0.05) -------------------------------------
df_donut <- df %>% filter(abs(running) > 0.05)
donut <- rdrobust(y = df_donut$Y, x = df_donut$running, c = 0)
summary(donut)
```
(Replace bandwidth and donut radius with context-specific values.)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Economic intuition usually predicts that receiving the treatment (e.g., a benefit, remedial class) should improve the outcome (e.g., income support raises consumption; tutoring raises test scores). I expect a positive local treatment effect of moderate size (e.g., 0.15–0.30 σ of the outcome, or ~5–10 percent increase).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Density of running variable is smooth at cutoff ………. 1  
C2: Observable covariates are continuous at cutoff ………. 1  
C3: Correct functional form & bandwidth robustness ……. 1  
C4: No manipulation/strategic sorting …………………….. 0 (uncertain)  
C5: Exclusion/monotonicity (fuzzy only) ……………….. 1  

Total = 4 / 5 → Overall strong but vigilance required on manipulation.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
This plan delivers a transparent, policy-relevant causal estimate exploiting the institutional threshold rule while explicitly testing and mitigating core threats to RDD validity.
